case.question: Compare Stephen Curry and LeBron James in the 2015-16 regular season on playmaking contributions and ball security. Use matched team on/off as context, not causal attribution.

answer:
# On-Court Impact Review

## Answer

**My position: the available evidence does not establish one overall on-court winner. The supported advantages and unresolved dimensions are separated below.**
- **Playmaking and ball security:** The indicators disagree; one player does not dominate all selected measures.
- **Team on/off context:** Regular Season: Stephen Curry has the higher on-minus-off net rating. This describes team association, not an isolated player effect.

This position compares observed contributions, not innate ability. Playmaking uses assists per minute and assists/turnovers, not a complete model of creation. Team on/off is association rather than causation.

**Scope:** 2015-16–2015-16 versus 2015-16–2015-16; Regular Season.

## Key evidence

- **Stephen Curry / 2015 / Regular Season**: Assists per 36 minutes **7.03** per 36 minutes; Assists per turnover **2.01** ratio. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **LeBron James / 2015 / Regular Season**: On-minus-off net rating **16.1** points / 100 possessions; ON min **2,709** minutes; OFF min **1,262** minutes. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612739&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=)
- **LeBron James / 2015 / Regular Season**: Assists per 36 minutes **6.83** per 36 minutes; Assists per turnover **2.06** ratio. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Stephen Curry / 2015 / Regular Season**: On-minus-off net rating **23.1** points / 100 possessions; ON min **2,700** minutes; OFF min **1,276** minutes. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612744&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=)

## Evidence by dimension

### Playmaking and ball security

| Player / phase | Metric | Value | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Stephen Curry / Regular Season | Recorded games (games) | 79 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| Stephen Curry / Regular Season | Minutes per game (per game) | 34.18 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| Stephen Curry / Regular Season | Assists per game (per game) | 6.67 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| Stephen Curry / Regular Season | Turnovers per game (per game) | 3.32 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| Stephen Curry / Regular Season | Assists per turnover (ratio) | 2.01 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| Stephen Curry / Regular Season | Assists per 36 minutes (per 36 minutes) | 7.03 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| LeBron James / Regular Season | Recorded games (games) | 76 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| LeBron James / Regular Season | Minutes per game (per game) | 35.64 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| LeBron James / Regular Season | Assists per game (per game) | 6.76 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| LeBron James / Regular Season | Turnovers per game (per game) | 3.28 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| LeBron James / Regular Season | Assists per turnover (ratio) | 2.06 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| LeBron James / Regular Season | Assists per 36 minutes (per 36 minutes) | 6.83 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |

## Team on/off evidence

Each row is a team-season and phase, not a career aggregate. Ratings are team points per 100 possessions. On-minus-off differences are not isolated player effects.

| Player / season / phase / team | On MIN | Off MIN | On ORtg | Off ORtg | On DRtg | Off DRtg | On Net | Off Net | Net difference | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| LeBron James / 2015 / Regular Season / Cleveland Cavaliers | 2,709 | 1,262 | 114 | 98.6 | 102.6 | 103.3 | 11.4 | -4.7 | 16.1 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612739&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=) |
| Stephen Curry / 2015 / Regular Season / Golden State Warriors | 2,700 | 1,276 | 117.5 | 102 | 99.8 | 107.4 | 17.7 | -5.4 | 23.1 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612744&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=) |

## Coverage and limits

- Historical box-score evidence is not equivalent to modern tracking or lineup data. Missing historical coverage does not count against a player.
- Steals, blocks and rebounds describe recorded activity; matchup difficulty, positioning, deterrence and defensive schemes are not measured here.
- On/off comparisons are confounded by lineup, opponent and substitution choices. No causal team/winning impact is established.
- Small or unequal appearance samples and stale API responses remain limitations. No synthetic overall impact score is used.

contract.claim: Compare Stephen Curry and LeBron James in the 2015-16 regular season on playmaking contributions and ball security using matched team on/off.

raw.answer:
Evaluating Stephen Curry and LeBron James during the 2016–17 regular season requires looking at two distinct architectural archetypes: Curry as the gravity-warping off-ball hub who orchestrated a historic offense, and LeBron as the traditional, high-usage primary point-forward who completely controlled the pace and distribution of his team. 

To contextualize their playmaking and ball security, we examine their raw production alongside **matched team on/off context**—specifically how their teams performed offensively with them on the court versus the bench, relative to similar lineup constructions.

---

### 1. Playmaking Contributions

#### **Stephen Curry: The Systemic Catalyst**
* **The Role:** While Curry was the nominal point guard, Golden State’s offense (guided by Steve Kerr) operated as a motion-heavy, egalitarian machine. Curry’s playmaking went far beyond traditional assists; it was driven by **gravity**. 
* **The Mechanics:** Curry led the league in scoring (30.1 PPG) on historic efficiency while averaging 6.7 assists. His unprecedented three-point range forced defenses to trap or double-team him 30 to 35 feet from the basket. This created 4-on-3 situations where Draymond Green or secondary playmakers could pick apart the defense. Curry’s relentless off-ball movement (running through multiple screens) manipulated defensive rotations, generating high-value teammate shots without necessarily touching the ball on the final pass.

#### **LeBron James: The On-Ball Orchestrator**
* **The Role:** LeBron operated as Cleveland’s undisputed offensive engine, averaging 25.3 PPG, 7.4 RPG, and 6.8 APG. His playmaking was much more direct, traditional, and heliocentric.
* **The Mechanics:** LeBron controlled the tempo entirely from the perimeter. Using elite pick-and-roll mastery and court vision, he routinely punished defenses that collapsed on his drives by firing skip passes to open shooters in the corners or dropping precise pocket passes to rolling big men. Unlike Curry’s off-ball burden, LeBron’s playmaking was almost entirely ball-dominant; the Cavaliers' offensive ecosystem relied on him initiating nearly every possession.

---

### 2. Ball Security

#### **Stephen Curry: High Creation, Elevated Turnover Risk**
* **Stats:** 3.3 Turnovers Per Game | ~15.5% Turnover Rate (TOV%)
* **Context:** Curry’s turnover numbers were a byproduct of his extreme offensive burden, high-risk passing style, and the sheer complexity of Golden State’s passing scheme. In attempting high-velocity, no-look, or tight-window passes within the motion offense, Curry frequently incurred live-ball turnovers. Furthermore, defenses aggressively trapped him in pick-and-rolls, forcing him into contested passing windows. 

#### **LeBron James: High Volume Control with Moderate Missteps**
* **Stats:** 3.3 Turnovers Per Game | ~14.3% Turnover Rate (TOV%)
* **Context:** Despite shouldering a massive possession share and heavy distribution duties, LeBron maintained a slightly better control-to-volume ratio than Curry. LeBron’s turnovers typically stemmed from over-penetration into packed paint defenses or ambitious cross-court reads. However, because he dictated the speed of the game, he was generally better able to dictate *when* and *where* he took risks compared to Curry's chaotic, fast-paced environment.

---

### 3. Matched Team On/Off Context

*Note: On/Off metrics measure net team performance differences when a player is on the floor versus the bench. These figures reflect total team context—including defensive performance, lineup combinations, and bench quality—and are used here strictly as environmental context rather than isolated causal proof of individual impact.*

* **Golden State Warriors (Curry On/Off):** 
  * The Warriors posted an offensive rating north of **114 to 115** with Curry on the floor during the regular season. 
  * When Curry sat, the Warriors' offense experienced a noticeable drop-off in efficiency and floor spacing, though Shaun Livingston and the bench units maintained a high-IQ, conservative style of play. Curry’s offensive on/off swing was among the highest in the league (+10 to +12 net differential), reflecting how deeply the Warriors' systemic identity relied on his unique offensive gravity.

* **Cleveland Cavaliers (LeBron On/Off):**
  * The Cavaliers featured a potent offense with LeBron on the floor, generally hovering around a **112 to 113** offensive rating.
  * When LeBron sat, Cleveland’s offense frequently stagnated into isolation-heavy possessions or struggled to generate efficient looks, resulting in a stark negative offensive rating drop in minutes without him. The Cavaliers' offensive dependency on LeBron was starker and more centralized than Golden State's dependency on Curry.

### Summary Comparison

| Metric / Dimension | Stephen Curry (2015-16) | LeBron James (2015-16) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Playmaking Style** | Off-ball gravity, motion disruption, and high-leverage passing out of traps. | On-ball dominance, pick-and-roll mastery, and drive-and-kick distribution. |
| **Assists / Usage** | 6.7 APG / ~32.6% USG | 6.8 APG / ~31.4% USG |
| **Ball Security** | 3.3 TPG (~15.5% TOV%) — higher risk due to pace and complex passing. | 3.3 TPG (~14.3% TOV%) — controlled tempo, deliberate distribution. |
| **Team Offensive Context** | Fueled a record-breaking 73-win system with massive on/off offensive elevation. | Carried a heliocentric offensive engine with severe drop-offs when resting. |
